name: subagent
description: Delegate a task to a subagent that has your full tool set. Use it when the work would flood this conversation with tool output (reading many files, paging through search results, long command runs), when independent pieces can run in parallel, or for a one-off investigation unrelated to the main thread. Coding work belongs here too: set dev=true and the subagent runs in development mode. The subagent runs in its own session with a fresh context and returns only one final message, so the prompt must be self-contained: background, conclusions you already confirmed, the goal, and what it should return. Use background=true for long tasks; you are woken when its whole task (including background jobs it started) finishes. It may delegate one level further, no deeper.

description.description: Short task description, used for progress display.

prompt.description: The complete task prompt for the subagent; it must stand on its own outside this conversation. The subagent cannot see your conversation history or anything the user said — include the background, constraints, and conclusions you have already found, and state explicitly what information it should return in its final reply.

dev.description: Run the subagent in development mode: the development system prompt plus a minimal coding tool set (commands, background jobs, patch editing, file search, todo, web). Turn it on for every coding task — writing, refactoring, debugging, reviewing, running builds and tests — and put the whole job in prompt, including which files and directories to work in.

max_steps.description: Optional cap on tool-call steps. Unlimited by default; the run ends when the task completes.

tier.description: Optional model tier by task difficulty: lite for trivial lookups and formatting, cheap for simple tool-using work, standard for regular multi-step work (default), flagship for hard reasoning. Every tier has the full tool set; an unconfigured tier falls back to the main model.

background.description: Run detached in the background: returns a job_id immediately, check with job(action=status); you are woken when the subagent's task finishes.

session_id.description: Optional. Continue an existing subagent (its session id from a previous result, or a background job_id): queued as a follow-up if it is still running, otherwise a new turn there with your prompt. Use it to steer or resume a subagent.

resume_id.description: Outside the daemon only: resume a run that failed with a resume_id in its error. Inside the daemon use session_id.
